previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), coronary artery disease with prior CABG, hypertension, and restless legs syndrome was re-admitted for acute dyspnea and fluid overload. She had been taking subtherapeutic doses of torsemide after a recent hospitalization, leading to an 8-pound weight gain and pulmonary edema. She was treated with intravenous diuresis, transitioned to oral torsemide 80 mg daily, and showed clinical improvement with resolution of hypoxia and normalization of BNP. A concurrent asymptomatic E. coli urinary infection was treated with antibiotics. Her restless legs symptoms persisted despite gabapentin uptitration, and IV iron was recommended post-discharge. She was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with strict instructions on weight monitoring and medication adherence.

successfully with 100 mg IV lasix x 3 days, 20 mg IV lasix x 1 
day, and then discharged on 40 mg po daily.  As she had a TTE 1 
month ago demonstrating an EF of 65%, this was not repeated.
